title: The role of ChatGPT in higher education: Benefits, challenges, and future research directions
extended_summary:
This paper examines the potential benefits and challenges of using ChatGPT in higher education, framed by constructivist theory of learning. Rather than reporting an empirical intervention, it offers a perspective on how generative AI may reshape teaching, learning, assessment, and academic support in tertiary settings. The authors organize the discussion around five perceived benefits and five major challenges, then propose 19 propositions for future research and institutional practice.

The paper treats ChatGPT as a general-purpose generative AI tool that can support adaptive learning, individualized feedback, research and writing assistance, automated administrative services, and innovative assessment design. In contrast, it identifies risks related to ethics and equity, academic integrity, bias and falsified information, limitations in assessing or reinforcing graduate skills, and difficulties in evaluating student learning outcomes. These issues are discussed in relation to constructivist ideas such as active learning, scaffolding, authentic assessment, and social interaction.

The population and context are higher education users, specifically students, academics/educators, and administrative staff in tertiary institutions. The paper does not study a specific intervention, sample, or outcome; instead, it argues that AI use should be paired with responsible-use education, redesigned assessments, and attention to fairness and reliability. Its main conclusion is that ChatGPT can enhance learning experiences in higher education, but only if institutions balance innovation with ethical safeguards and preservation of meaningful learning processes.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot based on GPT/LLM technology that can generate text, answer questions, provide feedback, and support personalized interactions.
identified_tools.use_case: Discussed as a generative AI tool in higher education, with proposed uses for adaptive learning, individualized feedback, research/writing support, automated administrative support, and innovative assessment activities; no empirical classroom study was reported.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a perspective/theoretical article rather than an empirical study. It proposes benefits, challenges, and propositions about ChatGPT but does not report a causal design, sample, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues that ChatGPT may support learning, feedback, and assessment, but it provides no effect sizes or outcome data. Impact is therefore speculative and based on conceptual discussion rather than demonstrated effects.
